problem.claim: Extend RoPE to support sequences longer than those used during pre-training.

gap.claim: Existing RoPE-extension strategies are diverse and lack a unified theoretical foundation.

contributions.claim: MrRoPE provides a generalized mixed-radix encoding formulation that unifies RoPE-extension approaches as radix-conversion strategies.
The paper introduces two training-free extensions, MrRoPE-Uni and MrRoPE-Pro, using uniform and progressive radix conversion for “train short, test long” generalization.

stated_novelty.claim: The proposed distinction is a radix-system conversion perspective that treats varied RoPE extensions as different radix-conversion strategies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, without fine-tuning, MrRoPE-Pro maintains over 85% recall on the 128K-context Needle-in-a-Haystack test.
The authors report that MrRoPE-Pro achieves more than twice YaRN’s accuracy on Infinite-Bench retrieval and dialogue subsets.
The authors report theoretical analysis indicating that MrRoPE-Pro raises the upper bound of RoPE’s attainable encoding length.

narrative_sequence.summary: RoPE extension modifies or generalizes RoPE to handle sequences longer than pre-training sequences.
Existing extension strategies are diverse without a unified theoretical foundation.
MrRoPE reframes extension methods through mixed-radix encoding and radix conversion.
MrRoPE-Uni and MrRoPE-Pro instantiate uniform and progressive radix conversion without training.
The authors report strong long-context retrieval results and a higher theoretical encoding-length upper bound for MrRoPE-Pro.

source_observation.claim: The abstract first identifies a fragmented strategy landscape, then introduces a unifying theoretical lens and derives two concrete variants from it.

lessons.interpretation: A unifying abstraction can make a method contribution easier to connect to both prior approaches and instantiated designs.
lessons.application: When presenting a family of techniques, define the shared formal perspective before introducing variants, and state which design choice differentiates each variant.
lessons.exception: This structure may be unsuitable when the proposed variants do not share a meaningful formal basis or when the paper’s contribution is purely empirical.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluation setup, dataset sizes, competing methods beyond YaRN, or statistical uncertainty for the reported results.
The theoretical claim is reported by the authors; the abstract does not provide the analysis details needed to assess its assumptions or derivation.
The abstract does not establish whether the reported gains generalize beyond the named tests and subsets.
